shouldFix: Easy share is too high: three of 15 are easy (r-p7-01:4 'run', r-p7-03:0 'address', r-p7-03:2 purpose) = 20% against the 8.3 target of at most 10%. Harden at least two: make one vocabulary distractor locally plausible, and tie the purpose distractors in r-p7-03:2 to facts that are actually in the documents. (Hard = 9 of 15 = 60%, so the hard target is met.)
Answer-position pattern: the second question of every set (r-p7-01:1, r-p7-02:1, r-p7-03:1) has key A, and D is the key only three times in 15. Reorder the options in at least one of those items.
r-p7-02:2: key 'have available for sale' is the longest option and the others are shorter; use one-word options (e.g. deliver / hold / stock / wear) as official word-meaning items do.
r-p7-03:2: key is the longest, only two-part option ('arrange a meeting and note new procedures'); equalize shape and length of the options.
r-p7-03:0: 'write a destination on' is an unnatural gloss of the address-an-envelope sense; rewrite.

r-p7-02 order form: the three line items are written as pipe-separated paragraphs ('Item DK-160 ... | Quantity: 6 | Color: oak'); an official order form would be a table (8.5 allows a table document), which also makes the arithmetic easier to find.

r-p7-03 optional: the ad says interviews run 'during the week of November 23' but Mr. Reyes is scheduled for November 30. The reply explains it only with 'Given the dates in your e-mail'. Plausible, not contradictory; one extra clause (e.g. 'the remaining slots that week are full') would remove the question.

r-p7-01:0: the key ('move to an event that ends earlier') is an inference rather than the way the e-mail frames its aim; acceptable, but a plainer key such as 'To request a change of workshop' would look more official (distractors would then need strengthening).
overall: These three sets look like official three-document sets in structure and tone: 435-467 words each including headers (inside 380-560), five questions in document order, official stems (What is indicated about / What is NOT indicated about / Where will ... most likely / In the second e-mail, the word 'x' in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to), short parallel options, e-mails with From/To/Date/Subject, and a table document in two of the three sets. Dates, weekdays, prices and arithmetic are consistent in all three (April 16 is a Thursday; Sept 22 Tuesday, Sept 25 Friday, Sept 14 Monday; Nov 30 Monday; order total $4,968, refund $222, $1,356 chairs under the $3,000 threshold; 'fifteen minutes later' gives 8:45), and every distractor I tried to rehabilitate fails on a document fact, so I found no ambiguous item and no internal inconsistency. Cross-document questions are similar to or somewhat harder than real triple passages because most combine a superseded plan with a correction plus a calculation (8:30+15, $37x6, Nov 26 vs Nov 21-25); the single-document purpose and word-meaning questions are about real-test level but come out easy under the rubric. Weak points: all three sets share one skeleton (original plan, a problem, a reply that changes the arrangements), the second question's key is A in every set, two options lists give the key away by length, and the document variety is narrower than a real exam (e-mail replies only, no text-message chain, review or invoice). Overall format fidelity is good (style about 4 of 5), difficulty is on the hard side for cross-document items and easy only for the vocabulary and purpose items.
